transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I came because I just feel so flat inside. Even when my children sit with me, or the sun is out on my garden, I can’t seem to feel glad or comforted. It’s like that part of me has just shut off.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About two weeks now. It started after my husband collapsed, and the paramedics were working on him right there in our kitchen. Since then I’ve felt this way.
Are you still able to enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable before your husband's collapse?

No, not really. Things I used to enjoy don’t feel the same now. Even when my children are with me, or I’m sitting where I can see the sun on my garden, I just feel flat. It’s like I can’t feel glad or comforted the way I used to.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself since your husband's collapse?
I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I haven’t been thinking clearly, but I don’t have anything specific to tell you about harming myself.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since your husband's collapse?
I’m not sure. I haven’t been weighing myself, and I haven’t really noticed my clothes fitting much differently.
Have you been feeling restless or having trouble sitting still, or has it been hard for you to get moving and do things?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself pacing or anything like that. Getting started with things is hard sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything since your husband's collapse?
I don’t really know. I’ve wondered if there was something I should’ve done differently, but I can’t say I’ve been feeling guilty in any clear way.
Have you been feeling like it's harder than usual to get moving and do things?

Yes. It’s been much harder. I don’t go to the senior center anymore, and I’m not really keeping up with things at home. My daughter has to help with meals, errands, and even my calendar. Most days I just stay in the house, and I don’t like going into the kitchen unless someone is with me.
Do you feel like your movements or reactions have slowed down since your husband's collapse?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed my movements being slower, exactly. I do feel like I have a hard time getting going, but I don’t know if my reactions are slower.
Have you been having any thoughts about wanting to harm yourself or end your life?
No... I don’t think so. I haven’t been thinking about hurting myself or ending my life.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?
Not really. Even when my children come and sit with me, or the sun is out on my garden, I just feel… flat inside. Things that should make me feel comforted or glad don’t really reach me now.
Do you feel like you've been moving more slowly than usual since your husband's collapse?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed myself moving slowly in particular. I just… I’m not paying much attention to that, I suppose.
Do you feel like it's been taking you longer than usual to complete everyday tasks?

Yes… I think so. It’s not so much that I’m moving slow, it’s that my mind just stops. I used to plan meals and keep my calendar straight without thinking, but now I’ll stare at a grocery list or the senior-center schedule and I can’t decide what to do. My daughter has to help me with simple things like that now.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight since your husband's collapse?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been checking my weight, and my clothes don’t seem much different that I’ve noticed.
Do you feel like you have been speaking more slowly than usual since your husband's collapse?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself talking slower than usual. Sometimes I pause because I’m trying to gather my thoughts, but I can’t say my speech itself is slower.
Do you feel like you've been fidgeting or feeling restless more often since your husband's collapse?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself fidgeting more. I do feel unsettled at times, but I couldn’t say I’m more restless than usual.
Have you been feeling jittery or fidgety since your husband's collapse?
I can’t really say that I have. I feel shaken at times, but I haven’t noticed myself being especially jittery or fidgety.
Have you lost a noticeable amount of weight since your husband's collapse?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been weighing myself, and I haven’t noticed my clothes fitting much differently. So I can’t say I’ve lost a noticeable amount.
Do you feel like you have been moving your body more slowly than you used to?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed myself moving slower than before. Maybe I’m a little tired sometimes, but I can’t say my body has slowed down in a clear way.
Do you feel like your body has been moving more slowly than usual since your husband's collapse?
Not that I’ve noticed, no. I’m tired, but I don’t feel like my body is moving unusually slowly or anything like that.
